transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SA), Maya Patel (StrataScale ML), Jordan Li (StrataScale Infra), Priya Nair (StrataScale PM)

Auto Summary: quick recap of last week's INT8 run, new FP8 baseline, a couple of regressions on long-form multi-turn, plan to run dedicated smoke test and share updated metrics.

[00:00] Alex (AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining on the 15th, um, quick roll call and then we'll jump in.
[00:12] Maya (ML Eng): hey loud and clear, Maya here. we got Jordan and Priya on.
[00:16] Jordan (Infra): yep here.
[00:20] Samira (SE): Samira from Redwood, I have the perf sheets up. quick note, some numbers were re-run this morning after the fix for KV cache eviction.
[00:30] Alex: cool, let's do a 2 min recap of results then dig into the regression cases.

[01:05] Samira: so summary first - INT8 run 2026-01-13 gives about 1.9x token throughput vs FP16 baseline at our standard batch, cost down ~44% on token units, p50 latency improved but p95 has a small increase, around +18-22% on long sequences. FP8 baseline from yesterday looks promising for throughput but shows slightly higher variance in the SNR metric we use for completion fidelity.

[02:10] Maya: what's the SNR again? sorry, sometimes the metric name gets swapped in our notes.
[02:14] Diego: it's the signal-to-noise—or our proxy for semantic fidelity—lower means more hallucination, uh we compute it from entailment scores over the prompt set.
[02:24] Maya: ok got it. the issue we saw on multi-turn earlier, is it the same one? responses becoming terse after turn three?

[03:00] Samira: yes that symptom. We traced it to two possible contributors: tokenization side-effects with int8 quant tables and the KV cache mismatch when prefix caching is off. when prefix cache is disabled, the runtime rebuilds keys which seems to amplify rounding.
[03:22] Jordan: does that mean our prefix caching in the prod-like bench was off? because our smoke-setup in our env had caching disabled for correctness checks.
[03:31] Samira: correct — your smoke runs had caching off on purpose, so we need to rerun with cache on to compare apples-to-apples.

[04:00] Priya (Product): quick question on deployment mode — are we still on hosted for the baseline or did Redwood spin up a dedicated pool for these runs?
[04:09] Alex: baseline INT8 and FP8 runs were on hosted but with dedicated-like instance types; we can run the dedicated pool smoke by next week per the plan.

[04:40] Maya: on hallucinations, I uploaded 40 failure examples to the shared drive, but I'll push another 160 that cover multi-turn, low-resource prompts, and the edge-case legalese.

[05:15] Samira: great, that helps. We'll run sensitivity sweeps over quant thresholds—per-layer scale tweaks and calibration windows. We think a per-layer calibration (couple layers) drops hallucination delta by ~0.8-1.2% in our internal tests.

[06:00] Speaker 4 (contractor?): one thing we noticed, the batching policy in your runtime — when it aggregates variable-length requests — p95 jumps. is that configurable at the client level?
[06:12] Diego: yes, we expose batching config via route policy; you can tune max batch size, max latency window, and prefer small-batches-for-latency. For the pilot, we recommend a two-tier policy: small-latency for interactive routes and large-batch for offline.

[06:40] Jordan: can that be per-model variant? our plan is to have an FP8 fallback and INT8 primary, so routing needs to be aware.
[06:49] Samira: yes routing supports tiered variants — we can do model-variant routing by priority and model compatibility. Automatic fallback also possible when capacity low.

[07:20] Maya: any notes on encryption/KMS when we go dedicated or on-prem? we need to confirm our compliance team that keys stay in our HSM.
[07:30] Alex: Redwood supports KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for Private installs. we'll share the security brief.

[08:05] Priya: will the logs have user-level traces for audit? SOC2 asks for retention details.
[08:12] Diego: yes, we can configure audit logs and retention windows. for the pilot we kept 30 days but enterprise can do longer.

[09:00] Samira: back to the perf deltas — attached link: spreadsheet/quant-probe-jan13.csv (note: link in notes). Important: one anomaly flagged — a subset of prompts with long numeric sequences under INT8 had token-level mistransforms, suspected due to the quant rounding in fast-float path.

[09:42] Maya: numeric sequences… that might impact our reports generator. we'll add 20 more examples focusing on numeric tables.

[10:15] Alex: can you describe the mismatch in more detail Samira? is it repeatable?
[10:20] Samira: somewhat repeatable — in about 2% of these long-numeric prompts the output swapped digits or truncated chunks. We think enabling subword-stability heuristics during detokenization reduces that by half. We'll push a patch to the tokeniser and rerun the INT8 trace.

[11:05] Jordan: side note — our infra wanted to know if the dedicated pool can be pinned to a region and if we can reserve capacity for the pilot window.
[11:14] Alex: yes we can pin region and reserve a small commit for the pilot week; we'll send options and pricing in the follow-up.

[12:00] Diego: also FYI we saw a small tail spike when KV cache misses went above 15% — this was in your smoke env where caching was off. So expectation: with caching on, p95 should normalize close to baseline.

[13:00] Maya: do you have a simple test harness to measure cache hit ratio? our team can run it locally.
[13:08] Samira: yes, we'll share a small python harness and a test script (link: github.com/redwood/mini-bench) with run instructions.

[14:00] Priya: on the quality metric, are we running human evals or only automated entailment checks?
[14:08] Maya: we did a small human eval batch of 100 but that method is expensive, so mainly automated plus a targeted human subset for regression.

[15:00] Samira: recommended next experiments: 1) INT8 with prefix caching on + tokeniser patch, 2) FP8 variant with per-layer calibration windows, 3) dedicated pool smoke test with two routing policies. We'll collect p50/p95, throughput, SNR delta, and hallucination examples.

[15:50] Maya: can you include memory usage deltas as well? our capacity planner needs that.
[15:55] Samira: yes memory and GPU util will be in the spreadsheet.

[16:30] Jordan: for the dedicated smoke, do you need us to open peering or will Redwood use a temporary VPN?
[16:37] Alex: VPC peering is easiest, Jordan. we'll provide CIDR ranges and the config. We'll also do a VPN option if you prefer.

[17:10] Priya: timeline wise — if we get the smoke by 1/20 and we like the deltas, can we plan a short on-prem feasibility review before EOD 1/27?
[17:19] Alex: that sounds doable. we'll tentatively pencil in 1/27 for an infra deep dive.

[18:00] Samira: quick note — competitor mention, Lambda did some public numbers that look close on throughput but they don't have the per-route observability we show. (murmurs)

[18:25] Maya: ok good to know.

[19:10] Diego: wrapping up — I'll enumerate concrete changes we'll run: tokeniser patch, per-layer INT8 calibration, FP8 alpha run, and dedicated smoke with caching on.

[20:00] Alex: let's capture action items — Samira will share updated micro-benchmarks by 1/20, Maya to upload full prompt set by 1/18, Jordan to spin up VPC peering test by 1/22. Also Redwood to share lane-level routing policy examples.

[20:45] Priya: any blockers from Redwood side we should be aware of?
[20:50] Samira: none immediate; we are waiting for your sample prompts and your green on peering.

[21:30] Maya: one last thing — can you include a short note on fallback behaviour if INT8 triggers a quality alert in prod? we'd like auto-fallback to FP8 for critical routes.
[21:45] Alex: yes that's standard — we can configure automatic variant fallback with alerts. we'll include a config snippet.

[22:10] Alex: great thanks everyone, we'll follow-up in email and share links to the updated sheets and harness. next sync same time next week unless we meet earlier for the infra deep dive.

Meeting end: 16:52 UTC

Links mentioned: spreadsheet: /quant-probe-jan13.csv; harness: github.com/redwood/mini-bench; security brief: redwood.com/security/brief (placeholder)

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions present, speaker overlap at times noted as 'Speaker 4'.
